_about: Mars overlay: replaces the Moon's milestone list (arrays replace). Ids are prefixed or distinct from the Moon's, because records are kept per campaign. Rules in rules/milestones.ts; zone sizes and the sunset band in data/mars/tuning.json milestones. Facts fact-checked November 15, 2026 (M5).
_interface: money and rp are placeholders set with Owner A. Sized so a run that drives, photographs or drills earns several times what a rover idling at the lander earns (Touchdown, perhaps Storm survivor).

milestones.name: Touchdown
milestones.summary: The rover has landed on the floor of Jezero crater and deployed from the lander.
milestones.fact: The Soviet Mars 3 lander made the first soft landing on Mars on December 2, 1971, but stopped transmitting within seconds; NASA's Viking 1 made the first lasting, successful landing on July 20, 1976.
milestones.source: NASA JPL, "NASA Mars Orbiter Images May Show 1971 Soviet Lander" (jpl.nasa.gov/news/nasa-mars-orbiter-images-may-show-1971-soviet-lander/); NASA Science, "Viking 1" (science.nasa.gov/mission/viking-1/)

milestones.name: Odometer
milestones.fact: Opportunity drove 45.16 km on Mars between 2004 and 2018, a record for another world until Perseverance passed it in October 2026.
milestones.source: NASA Science, "NASA's Perseverance Sets Off-World Record for Total Distance Driven" (science.nasa.gov/blogs/perseverance-mars-rover/2026/10/12/nasas-perseverance-sets-off-world-record-for-total-distance-driven/)

milestones.name: Mapper
milestones.summary: The rover has surveyed {share}% of the map.
milestones.fact: During its 2021 landing, Perseverance's Terrain-Relative Navigation matched descent-camera images to an onboard map made from Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter images, then steered toward a safe spot in Jezero.
milestones.source: USGS, "Mars 2020 Mission to be Guided by USGS Astrogeology Maps" (usgs.gov/news/mars-2020-mission-be-guided-usgs-astrogeology-maps)

milestones.name: Night drive
milestones.summary: Distance driven after dark, by the rover's own lights: {meters} m.
milestones.fact: Martian nights are brutally cold: Perseverance's weather station recorded lows near -83 °C at Jezero, so the rover keeps its electronics warm with heat from its nuclear power source and electric heaters.
milestones.source: NASA, "NASA's First Weather Report from Jezero Crater on Mars" (nasa.gov/feature/nasa-s-first-weather-report-from-jezero-crater-on-mars); NASA JPL, Mars 2020 press kit, "Power" (jpl.nasa.gov/news/press_kits/mars_2020/launch/mission/spacecraft/power/)

milestones.name: Storm survivor
milestones.summary: The dust storm has cleared and the rover is still operating.
milestones.fact: A 2018 planet-wide dust storm blocked sunlight to Opportunity, which last contacted Earth on June 10; NASA ended its mission on February 13, 2019. Nuclear-powered Curiosity kept working.
milestones.source: NASA JPL, "NASA's Opportunity Rover Mission on Mars Comes to End" (jpl.nasa.gov/news/nasas-opportunity-rover-mission-on-mars-comes-to-end/)

milestones.name: Delta layers
milestones.summary: The camera imaged the layered front of Jezero's ancient river delta.
milestones.fact: Perseverance's 2021 images of the 'Kodiak' butte showed delta layers laid down by a river flowing into a lake, confirming that Jezero once held a lake.
milestones.source: Mangold et al., Science 374 (2021), "Perseverance rover reveals an ancient delta-lake system and flood deposits at Jezero crater, Mars" (doi.org/10.1126/science.abl4051)

milestones.name: Core sample
milestones.summary: The drill collected a rock core, away from the ground the lander disturbed.
milestones.fact: Jezero's crater floor turned out to be volcanic rock; the lake's mud is in the delta, where in July 2022 Perseverance cored 'Wildcat Ridge' and SHERLOC detected the mission's most abundant organic molecules.
milestones.source: NASA JPL, "NASA's Perseverance Rover Investigates Geologically Rich Mars Terrain" (jpl.nasa.gov/news/nasas-perseverance-rover-investigates-geologically-rich-mars-terrain/)

milestones.name: Blue sunset
milestones.summary: The camera photographed the Sun setting over Jezero crater.
milestones.fact: Curiosity photographed a blue sunset in Gale crater on April 15, 2015 (sol 956): fine dust in Mars' air lets blue light pass through more efficiently, so blue stays closer to the Sun.
milestones.source: NASA JPL, "Sunset in Mars' Gale Crater" (science.nasa.gov/photojournal/sunset-in-mars-gale-crater)
